tasks.title: Chat input images and dismiss focus
tasks.prompt:
Work in the managed firstmate-3000 repo (adopted checkout). Delivery is direct-pr: land on a local branch, push, open a pull request. Do not merge. Autonomy is off.

Two related chat-input changes. Do both in one PR.

## 1. Focus the chat input after dismissing a card

After the user dismisses a card, keyboard focus must return to the home VoiceInput (the task prompt), so they can type the next turn without clicking.

What “dismiss” means here: any user action that removes the currently shown card from the visible stack (Done / dismiss on notes and task-results, acting on a decision so the card leaves, discarding a task, etc.). When the stack still has cards, focus the input only if that is still the calm next step; when the last visible card is gone and the shell returns toward idle/thinking, the input must be focused.

Do not steal focus when:
- the action opens Settings
- VoiceInput is in recording mode
- the user is in the Settings view

Wire this in the renderer shell (`src/renderer/src/app/store.ts`, `HomeScreen.tsx`, `VoiceInput`) without breaking the existing rule that CardLayer is the only subscriber to streaming card bodies (do not re-render Firstmate/VoiceInput on body ticks). Prefer a small, explicit focus seam (ref / callback) over polling.

Cover with a unit or component test, and an e2e assertion if there is an existing card-dismiss path that is cheap to extend.

## 2. Paste images into the Firstmate chat input

The main Firstmate agent must accept images pasted into the home chat input. This is a product/design change, not a hidden power-user hook.

Design first, then implement:
- All UI must follow `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/`. If the skill has no rule for attachments, chips, or a non-pill expansion of VoiceInput, extend the skill first (VoiceInput.prompt.md / .d.ts, readme product concepts, click-through mock under `ui_kits/firstmate/` if the idle/listening states change), then implement in `src/renderer/src/design/voice/VoiceInput.tsx` and the production host.
- Keep the calm single-input null state. Voice activation stays keybind-only. No chat bubbles. Sentence case, no emoji, tokens only (no raw hex/px the adherence lint forbids).
- Pasting (⌘V / Ctrl+V) an image while the input is focused must attach it. Show a small, obvious preview/chip so the user knows the image will go with the next send. They must be able to remove an attached image before send. Text + images together are allowed. Enter / the existing submit control sends text and attachments.
- Empty text with only images is a valid send.
- Reasonable types: png, jpeg, gif, webp. Reject or ignore non-images quietly; do not crash on huge clips — cap size and say so in the feed or a short notice if you must surface failure.

End-to-end through the Firstmate agent (not crewmates):
- Today `fm:converse` / `window.firstmate.conversation.send` is a single string (`src/shared/ipc.ts`). The frozen `window.firstmate` surface and Firstmate tool set are pinned in `tests/e2e/phase0-guardrails.spec.ts` and `scripts/generate-self-source.mjs` (+ its test). If you extend the converse payload, update those pins deliberately and keep existing `send(text)` callers working.
- `FirstmateAgent.converse` and `FirstmateSession.prompt` / `steer` currently take text only. Investigate how `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` `AgentSession.prompt` accepts images (do not invent a side channel the model never sees). Persist attachments across the steer-if-busy path the same way text does. The rolling session must still survive restarts for text; images on a live unsent compose can stay in renderer memory.
- Do not send image bytes through the activity feed or card bodies.

## Constraints

- Green gate before you push: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test`, then `pnpm build && pnpm exec playwright test` for e2e you touch or that could regress home/input.
- Do not modify packaged self-source generation output except as required by the existing generate-self-source pin contract.
- No new user-facing concepts (no “attachments panel”, no settings toggle unless strictly required).
- Match existing copy voice: sentence case, factual, no exclamation points.

## Acceptance

- Dismissing a card returns focus to the task prompt (except Settings / recording cases above).
- Pasting an image into the focused input shows a designed preview; submit delivers that image to the Firstmate turn; user can remove it before send.
- Design skill and mock stay the source of truth for the new VoiceInput states.
- PR opened against the default branch; CI-ready; not merged.

tasks.title: Remove the task-result card kind
tasks.prompt:
Work in firstmate-3000. Delivery direct-pr: branch, push, open a PR. Do not merge.

## Task

Completely remove the `task-result` card kind. It is the card that currently wraps every crewmate turn with fixed chrome (Discard / Land this work / Done). That chrome is not a real decision and the report body is not authored as one.

Replace it with the two cards that already exist:
- **decision** — when a merge/land (or any real choice) is needed. The body must state the question and what each option does. Later is still prepended by the app.
- **note** — when the user just needs an update worth seeing. One fact, no fake Land/Done pair. App adds Done if no actions.

## Current behavior to delete

- `cardKindSchema` includes `"task-result"` (`src/shared/cards.ts`). D-9 taxonomy.
- Supervisor creates a streaming `task-result` at spawn and fills it from the crewmate’s final assistant text (`crewSupervisor.ts` `startTask` / `turnComplete` / `finish`). Ready cards always get `taskCardActions()`: Discard task, Land this work, Done.
- `act()` treats `dismiss` on `kind === "task-result"` as decommission of an idle crewmate.
- Crewmate prompt (`buildCrewmateSystemPrompt`) and `docs/card-authoring.md` say the final report automatically becomes a task-result card.
- Renderer maps `task-result` → ResponseCard `"result"` (`HomeScreen.tsx`).
- Pins: `src/shared/cards.test.ts`, `scripts/generate-self-source.mjs` (+ its test), e2e that click “Land this work” (`tests/e2e/workspace-inference.spec.ts` and any other), supervisor tests that assert `kind === "task-result"`.
- Design skill copy that treats “task result” as a first-class card kind (readme product concepts, ResponseCard if needed). Update the skill to match: cards are decision, note, live-prototype.

## New behavior

1. **No automatic report card.** A crewmate’s final assistant text must not become a card. It already reaches the feed (`task_report`) and Firstmate’s inbox. That is enough for routine turn-end. Emitting zero cards is correct when nothing needs the user.

2. **No streaming task card.** Working state is the Firstmate character + feed. Do not stream a blank note. Notes are never progress updates.

3. **Merge/land is a decision card.** When the user must choose whether to land work into the repo checkout, raise a `decision` whose body names the repo, branch, and what will happen. Suggested actions (sentence case, kebab-case ids): land into the current checkout (this is `landTaskWork` — local ff/merge, not merging the GitHub PR), leave the branch/PR as-is, discard if destructive discard is in play. Labels must say the actual effect (“Merge into the current checkout”, not “Land this work”). Wire `land` through the existing `landTaskWork` path.

   Who raises it:
   - Crewmates and Firstmate emit it via `emit_card` when they need a merge decision (update both system prompts).
   - If autonomy is off and a turn ends with unlanded commits or dirty work and that task has no open decision card, the supervisor must raise this decision itself so the captain is never left without a way to land. If autonomy is on, existing auto-land behavior stays if one exists; do not invent new silent merges.

4. **Updates are notes.** Crewmate/Firstmate `emit_card` kind note only when there is one fact the user must see. Dismissing a note must not decommission the crewmate.

5. **Task lifecycle without Done.** Idle multi-turn stays. Decommission/complete happens by: landing (existing deleteTask), discard, `interrupt_crewmate` cancel, or a decision action that explicitly closes the task (include this on the land decision as “leave the branch and close the task” if after_task gates would otherwise stick). Do not hide decommission behind a button labeled Done.

6. **emit_card schema** (`src/main/pi/cardTool.ts`): drop `task-result` from allowed kinds. Update generate-self-source pins and any Firstmate prompt text that lists kinds.

7. **Renderer / design.** ResponseCard may keep a visual `"result"` tone internally if useful, but there is no `task-result` kind to map. Priority order in tests: decision > live-prototype > note.

## Constraints

- Do not regress live-prototype or Firstmate-emitted decision/note cards.
- Card copy: sentence case, factual, no exclamation points, no emoji.
- Parallel tasks are editing VoiceInput/HomeScreen (image paste, focus). Touch those only if the card-kind map in HomeScreen requires it; keep the conflict tiny.
- Green: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test`, plus Playwright for e2e you change (workspace-inference and any card-stack specs).
- Update AGENTS.md / docs/architecture.md D-9 / card-authoring only as needed so they stop documenting task-result as current.
- Open a PR. Do not merge.

## Acceptance

- `task-result` is gone from the schema, emit_card, prompts, supervisor, renderer mapping, and pins.
- A finished crewmate turn with nothing to decide produces no task-result card (feed/inbox only, optional note if they emit one).
- A land/merge choice is a decision card whose options match what the buttons do.
- Existing land/discard/after_task behavior still works through those decision actions.
- Tests rewritten, not deleted, for the new kinds.

tasks.title: Define CI green as the full suite
tasks.prompt:
Work in firstmate-3000. Delivery direct-pr. Prefer updating open PR 8 (`fm/task-e6f89e45`, https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate-3000/pull/8) rather than a new PR. Do not merge.

## Change

In the crewmate prompt, Firstmate prompt, spawn_crewmate tool text, and AGENTS.md standing rule added by PR 8, state explicitly:

- CI is green only when every check on the PR **head commit** has `status=completed` and `conclusion=success`.
- A pass on the job named `checks` is not enough if `package-smoke` (or any other check) is pending, skipped-as-required, or failed.
- Older failed runs on earlier SHAs do not count once the head is fully green; conversely, a green job on an old SHA does not make the PR green.
- Firstmate must verify with `gh pr checks` (or the check-runs API) before saying green or raising a land/merge decision. If anything is pending, wait or steer; do not report green.

Babysit this PR’s own CI the same way: wait until every check on the head SHA is success before reporting ready. Do not merge.

## Acceptance

- Prompts/docs cannot be read as “the checks job passed, therefore green.”
- PR 8 (or a follow-up PR) updated; full suite green on the head commit.

cards.title: Proposal: instant feedback on card actions, and on every button
cards.body:
The full proposal, for reading here. It also sits on branch fm/task-dc0f3437 as docs/card-action-feedback.md, but nothing needs to be merged to read it.

What happens today

Card actions fall into two classes, and only one of them feels like a click.

ClassExamplesWhat the click doesTime to a visible change
Steer / dismissLater, Done, Start anyway, any crewmate optionDeletes the card, resolves it, rebroadcastsabout 60ms
Host-owned settleLand locally, Merge PR, DiscardKeeps the card up, fires the operation unawaitednone, until the work finishes

Three facts from the code. The renderer's actOnCard fires the IPC and changes no local state, so nothing knows a click happened. The steer path feels instant only because act() happens to delete the card before returning — an ordering accident, not a rule. And the settle path is slow on purpose: it holds the card "until the landing settles" while gh pr checks and gh pr merge run at a 30-second timeout each, followed by the worktree teardown. Throughout, every button stays enabled.

The part that is worse than slow

Land, merge and discard are fail-closed by contract: they never mint a card, they return their reason as a string so the caller decides. The Firstmate tool path honors that. The card path drops it with void.

  • Merge blocked because CI is red: reason discarded, card stays, nothing said. Indistinguishable from a dead button.
  • Discard refused because the worktree has unlanded commits: the same silence.
  • Because the buttons stay live, a second click issues a second gh pr merge against the same PR.

The principle

Every button commits within one frame. A click must change the surface it was on before the next paint. What it sets in motion may take sixty seconds; the acknowledgement may not.

Three legal responses, in preference order:

  1. Resolve-and-close (default). The surface closes or commits at once, the work continues in the background, the outcome arrives through a channel that outlives the card.
  2. Commit-in-place. The control shows its new state immediately — a toggle flips, a row updates.
  3. Pending-in-place. Only when you must stay and see the result inline. The clicked control disables and swaps its label, and the whole row disables so no sibling can be clicked.

Never legal: a click that leaves the surface unchanged while an await runs.

The corollary matters as much as the rule. The acknowledgement is not the outcome. Closing the card is a receipt for the click, not a claim that the merge succeeded. So every backgrounded operation owes you an outcome through something that survives the card: the activity feed for the routine path, a fresh card for the failure path.

Applied to the settle actions

ActionImmediateBackgroundFailure
Merge PRcard closesCI check, merge, teardownnew card with the reason
Land locallycard closesgit merge, teardownnew card with the reason
Discardcard closesstatus check, teardownnew card offering Discard anyway

Concretely: act() removes and resolves the card the moment the action arrives — the same three lines the steer path already runs — then hands the operation to a tracked background runner. A per-task in-flight guard refuses a second settle instead of starting a second merge, which matters more once the card closes instantly and you can reach the next card. A new feed line narrates the work while it runs. And the reason string that is dropped today becomes a decision card with a stable id, carrying the reason verbatim and offering the retry.

The dirty-discard path needs no new machinery: the refusal surfaces as that failure card, offering Discard anyway, which already exists and already resolves instantly.

The renderer safety net

The renderer should not depend on the core being fast. A per-card pending action in the shell store, set synchronously before the IPC await, lets the action row disable and the clicked button show pending. That makes mode 3 the automatic fallback for any action that turns out to be slow — including ones nobody has thought of yet — while mode 1 wins the race whenever the core is fast. They never conflict: if the card is gone within 60ms the pending state was never painted. Holding the pending paint for about 120ms, under the fast motion duration, keeps quick clicks from flickering.

Making it hold for all buttons

A principle stated only in prose decays. Three layers:

  1. Component. A pending prop on the shared Button: disables, holds its layout width so the row does not reflow, swaps the label. The one place doing this by hand today — the Connect button's "Connecting..." — folds into it.
  2. Rule. The design skill has no latency or feedback rule at all right now, which is exactly why this is unenforced. It gets one, alongside the motion guideline, plus the new prop in the Button reference.
  3. Lint. The adherence config already enforces per-component prop allowlists through AST selectors. The same mechanism carries a rule that flags an async onClick: "must give instant feedback: close the surface, or pass pending to the control." Deliberately blunt; the escape hatch is a scoped disable with a reason. Blunt and noisy is the right trade for a rule whose failure mode is silent.

Crewmate-authored card bodies raise their actions through the sandbox bridge into the same handler, so they inherit the behavior without a separate rule.

Not proposed

  • A toast system. The activity feed is already the designated place for background narration, and it persists. A second ephemeral channel would compete with it.
  • Optimistic rollback that re-opens the same card. A failure gets a new card with the reason. Restoring a card you believe you dismissed is harder and less honest.
  • Changing the card-action IPC channel. The transport is fine. The latency is in what act() chooses to await.

Residual risk: closing the card first means a merge failure arrives as a second interruption a few seconds later. The feed line firing immediately is the mitigation — the failure card is then a follow-up, not the first news that anything was happening.

Rollout

StepPinned by
1. Background the settle actions; add the in-flight guardcard gone before the operation resolves; second click refused
2. Failure card carrying the dropped reasona blocked merge mints a card with the reason
3. Settling event and feed linesfeed mapping test
4. Renderer pending stateset synchronously, cleared on resolve
5. Button pending prop; migrate Connectadherence lint, component test
6. Adherence rule and the project memory linethe adherence lint run

Steps 1 and 2 are worth doing regardless of the rest: they fix a silent failure, not only a slow one.

Three questions for you

  • Feed wording for the in-flight lines — "merging PR - title", or something quieter.
  • Should the merge-failure card offer a re-check action that re-runs the CI check, or only a plain retry?
  • Should the 120ms pending delay become a motion token in the design skill, or stay a local constant?

The rule lives in src/shared/nowPanel.ts:42-55 (function nowGroupOf), restated identically in src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/now/now.frame.js and pinned in sync by tests/e2e/now-panel.spec.ts.

There is no check on git/PR/CI state anywhere in the path that sets status = "delivered". It is a pure process-completion signal: the crewmate stopped running, nothing more.

The transition itself — src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.ts:1992-1993:

if (status === "completed") {
  this.options.tasks.close(taskId, { status: "delivered", reason: "finished", actor });
}

How a crewmate becomes "idle" enough to finish — the settle_task "finish" mode, crewSupervisor.ts:1819-1825, checks only that the crewmate isn't mid-turn:

if (runtime.state !== "idle") {
  return `Cannot finish task ${taskId} while it is still working...`;
}
this.finish(runtime, "completed");

No call to git status, no PR lookup, no CI read. Compare this to the "discard" branch a few lines down (crewSupervisor.ts:1860-1868), which does check for uncommitted edits or unlanded commits via workspace.taskWorkStatus before allowing a drop — that guard exists only for discard, not for finish/deliver.

The close itself — src/core/tasks/taskService.ts:1048-1063 (close()) just patches whatever status it's handed:

this.patch(id, {
  status: input.status,
  activity: null,
  closedReason: input.reason,
  closedAt: at,
  ...
});

No validation logic lives here either.

cards.title: Who writes delivered, and how active would stick
cards.body:
Deterministic host code writes the status. Neither Firstmate nor a crewmate can set status to a string. The one writer is TaskService.close in src/core/tasks/taskService.ts (around 1048). Agents only choose a tool or a card action; the supervisor maps that onto close.

The mapping

CrewSupervisor.closeRecord in src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.ts (1986–1993) is the only product path that asks for delivered:

  • wire completed → stored delivered, reason finished
  • cancelled / failed → dropped

Opening a PR does not do this. PrCiService.record in src/core/orchestrator/prCi.ts (210–232) only patches delivery.prUrl / delivery.ci via recordDelivery. CI pending is a delivery fact on whatever status the row already has.

What can trigger completed → delivered

  1. settle_task mode finish — Firstmate tool in src/core/pi/crewTools.ts (256–268), wired in firstmateAgent.ts (747–749), handled at settleTaskOnce (1819–1824). The agent picks finish; the host decommissions. No CI check.
  2. Done on a task-result card — act() (2910–2918) and taskCardActions (3114–3118). Captain click; host calls finish(..., "completed"). No CI check.
  3. Cancel on an idle crewmate that already reported — interruptCrewmate (1144–1148, 1162–1163) plus idleCancelStatus (1181–1182). Treated as decommission, not abort.
  4. finish() itself (1581–1582) when the runtime is torn down while the row is still open or active.

Keep on a settle card does not write delivered. act() (2920–2923) leaves the crewmate idle and the record active.

Migration and test fixtures also map old completed → delivered when a worktree exists (src/core/storage/db.ts mapLegacyStatus, src/core/tasks/seedTask.ts). Not a live path.

How “change it to active” would work

We would not add a “set status active” tool, and we would not ask the agent to pick a status. Active is the default while a crewmate exists. The change is: do not call closeRecord(..., "completed") on a direct-pr row whose delivery.ci is pending, red, or unchecked.

  • Finish / Done / idle-cancel would refuse with text, same as finish already refuses a streaming crewmate (1822–1824). The row stays active because it never closed.
  • Firstmate would keep steering (prompt already says not-green → steer, no captain card: src/core/pi/piResources.ts ~82). That is policy on top of the gate, not a second writer.
  • Merge-pr and discard stay as they are. Merge already re-checks CI in PrCiService.merge.
  • Rows already delivered with ci pending would not be auto-reopened. Display-only: taskStatusWord in src/shared/nowPanel.ts would say CI pending instead of to land. Reopening is a different, larger change.

Nothing will be edited until you approve a change.

A failure card is more visible and actionable than a feed line, as long as it reuses a stable per-task id (e.g. `card-<taskId>-merge-failed`) so repeated attempts update the same card in place instead of stacking duplicates. I'd give it two actions: "Retry merge" and "Keep open" (dismiss).

By the time a Merge PR card is shown at all, Firstmate is already supposed to have confirmed fresh-green CI (per the existing contract — it steers the crewmate to fix red/pending CI before ever presenting a decision), so most click-time failures are either transient (`gh` network/API hiccup) or durable (head moved since the check, branch protection, a parent-task block). Transient errors are safe to retry automatically a couple of times with backoff inside the merge call itself. Durable ones aren't safe to auto-retry — they need a fresh CI re-check or a human decision, which is exactly what a "Retry merge" button on the failure card gives you, without the system taking merge actions the captain didn't click.
